title: Dune: Part Two
description: The sequel to Denis Villeneuve Dune adaptation. Paul unites with the Fremen to wage war against House Harkonnen while the prophecy of the Lisan al-Gaib tightens around him. A colossal sci-fi epic shot like a painting, with a score that shakes the room.
legacyCastNotes: Timothée Chalamet trained for months with a fight and movement coach to move like a Fremen warrior.
Zendaya's Chani was expanded massively from the book — she is the film's moral compass.
Hans Zimmer composed the score partly on a custom-made instrument built from broken cellos.
The sandworms are rendered with a mix of practical miniature dunes and CGI — no real worm was harmed.
teaser: Paul Atreides faces the desert, the prophecy, and his own destiny. The sandworms are coming, and so is war.
facts: The desert scenes were shot on location in Jordan and Abu Dhabi with real dunes, no green screen.
The sandworm riding sequence took over three months of rehearsal with a custom gimbal rig.
Hans Zimmer reportedly turned down other projects for years to focus on this score.
Chani, played by Zendaya, appears far more in the film than in the book.

title: Top Gun: Maverick
description: Tom Cruise returns as Pete Maverick Mitchell, now a test pilot forced to train a new generation for an impossible mission. Shot with real jets and real G-forces, it is the rare legacy sequel that outflies the original.
legacyCastNotes: Tom Cruise performed the jet sequences himself, enduring up to 7.5 Gs.
Miles Teller spent months learning to fly so his cockpit scenes look real.
The cast trained in actual F/A-18s with real Top Gun instructors.
Cruise insisted the film use no CGI for flight — everything you see was filmed.
teaser: Thirty years later, Maverick is back with one more mission. The sky has never felt closer.
facts: The actors really flew in F-18s and endured up to 7.5 Gs during filming.
There is no CGI for the flight scenes, only practical aerial cinematography.
Maverick is the only Tom Cruise film where he actually plays a father figure to his rival son.
The final canyon run was filmed in real locations, not a set.

title: Oppenheimer
description: Christopher Nolan epic about J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the Manhattan Project. A three-hour thunderclap that turns committee rooms into battlefields and a physics lecture into a horror film.
legacyCastNotes: Cillian Murphy lost roughly 20 pounds to play the gaunt physicist.
The Trinity explosion was created practically — no CGI.
Nolan wrote the script in first person so the audience sees through Oppenheimer's eyes.
Robert Downey Jr. wore prosthetics and grey hair to play Lewis Strauss.
teaser: The man who built the bomb. The moment that ended the world and began his.
facts: The Trinity test was recreated without CGI, using practical explosives and lighting tricks.
The film is told in two timelines distinguished by color and black and white.
Cillian Murphy lost a significant amount of weight for the role.
The script was written in the first person, so the audience sees what Oppenheimer sees.

title: Godzilla Minus One
description: Set in postwar Japan, a kamikaze pilot returns home to a destroyed country and faces a new terror rising from the sea. It became the first Japanese Godzilla film to win an Oscar.
legacyCastNotes: Director Takashi Yamazaki did much of the VFX himself on his home computer.
The film cost about $15 million — a fraction of a Hollywood blockbuster.
Godzilla's design returns to the original 1954 silhouette.
The Oscar win for VFX made it the first Japanese Godzilla film to win an Academy Award.
teaser: Japan, post-war, zero hope. And then the sea begins to move. The best Godzilla film in decades.
facts: It won the Oscar for Best Visual Effects on a budget of about 15 million dollars.
The film is set in 1945-1947, right after World War Two.
The director also wrote and edited the film and handled much of the VFX himself.
The monster design returns to the original 1954 silhouette.

title: Interstellar
description: Nolan most emotional film. As Earth dies, a farmer turned pilot leads a mission through a wormhole to find a new home for humanity, while his daughter waits on Earth. A three-hour ode to fathers, daughters, and the idea that love might be physics.
legacyCastNotes: Matthew McConaughey insisted on real cornfields — the crew grew 500 acres of corn for the opening.
Hans Zimmer wrote the score before seeing the script, based on one page of notes.
The black hole Gargantua was simulated with real physics equations.
TARS the robot was operated by puppeteers — zero CGI.
teaser: Mankind last hope is a wormhole, a ship, and a father who refuses to say goodbye. Love is the only thing that crosses dimensions.
facts: Hans Zimmer wrote the score before seeing the script, based on a one-page description.
The wormhole and black hole visuals were generated with real physics equations.
The cornfield scenes were filmed in a real field that had just been harvested for the production.
The TARS robot was operated by puppeteers, not CGI.

title: Avengers: Endgame
description: The epic conclusion to the Infinity Saga. The remaining Avengers attempt a time heist to undo the Snap. A three-hour blockbuster that somehow balances spectacle, comedy, and grief.
legacyCastNotes: Robert Downey Jr.'s final scene was kept secret from most of the cast.
The film was shot almost entirely with code names like 'Mary Lou' to stop leaks.
The final battle features over 60 heroes on screen at once.
At $2.79 billion, it was the highest-grossing film ever until Avatar returned.
teaser: Half of all life is gone. The survivors have one chance, and they will not waste it.
facts: It was the highest-grossing film of all time at release, over 2.7 billion dollars.
The final battle featured dozens of heroes and took months of coordination.
The title was kept secret during production to avoid leaks.
The iconic portals scene was kept under wraps until the premiere.

title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
description: After his identity is revealed, Peter asks Doctor Strange to make the world forget, and the spell goes wrong, pulling villains from other universes into his world. A love letter to twenty years of Spider-Man on screen.
legacyCastNotes: The three Spider-Men were hidden with secret trailers and NDAs.
Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield filmed their scenes separately from Tom Holland.
The film's title was kept secret — even the cast didn't know it until the first teaser.
Willem Dafoe wore the original Green Goblin mask from 2002.
teaser: Peter Parker wants his secret back. Instead, he tears a hole in the multiverse and everything he loves walks through it.
facts: The film broke pandemic box office records, grossing nearly two billion dollars.
The three Spider-Men were kept secret and their scenes filmed with heavy security.
Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield had to sign strict non-disclosure agreements.
The villains all return from their original films with the same actors.

title: The Batman
description: A noir take on the Dark Knight in his second year. Batman hunts the Riddler, a serial killer targeting Gotham elite, and uncovers a corruption web that reaches the city foundations. Robert Pattinson broods like never before.
legacyCastNotes: Robert Pattinson wore a Batsuit that he could barely turn his head in — by design, for the noir feel.
The Batmobile is a real car, built on a 1963 Ford Galaxie chassis.
Paul Dano's Riddler mask was inspired by real serial-killer obsession.
The film was shot almost entirely at night in the rain — 96 nights of filming.
teaser: He is vengeance. But Gotham needs more than vengeance, it needs a detective.
facts: The Batmobile was built around a real car chassis and can actually drive.
The film is heavily inspired by noir classics and the Long Halloween comic.
The Riddler design was inspired by real serial killers and zodiac letters.
The Batman was filmed almost entirely at night in rainy conditions.

title: Avatar: The Way of Water
description: James Cameron thirteen-year sequel. Jake and Neytiri flee into the oceans of Pandora, where a new clan teaches their children to swim, breathe, and fight. A three-hour water epic that had to invent new technology to film underwater motion capture.
legacyCastNotes: The cast trained to hold their breath for up to 7 minutes underwater.
Kate Winslet's breath-hold set a record for the production — over 7 minutes.
Cameron waited 13 years for underwater motion-capture tech to be invented.
The water in the film is 100% computer-generated around real performances.
teaser: The sky people are back. The Sully family must leave the forest and learn to live under the sea.
facts: The cast trained to hold their breath for minutes to film underwater scenes.
Cameron waited over a decade for the technology to film underwater motion capture.
The film grossed over 2.3 billion dollars worldwide.
The water is fully computer generated around real performances.

title: The Matrix Resurrections
description: Lana Wachowski returns alone for a self-aware sequel. A game designer named Thomas Anderson starts having dreams about a world he once saved. Meta, strange, and unmistakably its own thing.
legacyCastNotes: Keanu Reeves did most of his own stunts, including the famous rooftop jump.
The film was Lana Wachowski's first directed alone — Lilly sat it out.
The 'bullet time' was achieved with 120 still cameras in a circle.
Carrie-Anne Moss did her own motorcycle stunt work.
teaser: The Matrix is back, and Neo does not know who he is. The truth is still out there, buried in a blue pill.
facts: It is the first Matrix film directed by only one Wachowski.
The film openly makes fun of studio sequels and its own legacy.
Keanu Reeves and Carrie-Anne Moss reprise their roles after two decades.
The film was shot in San Francisco and Berlin.

title: Barbie
description: Greta Gerwig billion-dollar meditation on womanhood, packaged as a pink comedy. Barbie leaves her perfect world, enters the real one, and brings the patriarchy question back to Barbie Land.
legacyCastNotes: The production used so much pink paint that it depleted the world supply of a specific brand.
Ryan Gosling's Ken was written for him — Greta Gerwig had him in mind from page one.
Margot Robbie did her own rollerblading and dance scenes.
America Ferrera's monologue was shot in one long take.
teaser: In Barbie Land, every day is perfect. Until Barbie asks: what happens if I think about dying?
facts: It grossed over 1.4 billion dollars, the highest for a female-directed film.
The film used so much pink paint that it caused a global shortage of a specific shade.
Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling both earned Oscar nominations.
America Ferrera monologue became one of the most discussed scenes of the decade.

title: Dune
description: The first half of Villeneuve epic adaptation. House Atreides takes control of Arrakis, the only source of the galaxy most valuable substance, and walks into a trap. The foundation for the masterpiece that followed.
legacyCastNotes: The Sardaukar battle language was invented by linguist David Peterson.
The sandworm's inner teeth were inspired by a whale's mouth.
Oscar Isaac and Jason Momoa improvised several of their buddy scenes.
The stillsuit design went through over 50 iterations.
teaser: A desert planet. A spice that rules the galaxy. A young duke who must become something more than a man.
facts: The sandworm design was refined over a year of concept work.
The film won six Oscars for its technical craft.
The desert scenes were shot in Jordan and the UAE.
The Sardaukar language was constructed specifically for the film.

title: No Time to Die
description: Daniel Craig final Bond film. A retired Bond is called back when a scientist goes missing and a new bioweapon threatens the world. A fitting, emotional send-off for the best Bond era in decades.
legacyCastNotes: Daniel Craig performed the stairwell fight scene himself, breaking ribs twice.
The opening gun-barrel sequence took 400 takes to get right.
Billie Eilish was the youngest artist ever to record a Bond theme.
The film gives Bond a daughter — a franchise first.
teaser: The world is on the edge. Bond is pulled out of retirement for one last mission, and nothing will ever be the same.
facts: It is the longest Bond film ever made, at 163 minutes.
The theme song by Billie Eilish made her the youngest artist to record a Bond theme.
The film had one of the longest delays in cinema history due to the pandemic.
It is the first Bond film to give Bond a child.

title: Tenet
description: Nolan inversion thriller. A secret agent learns to fight through time itself, where bullets un-fire and buildings un-explode. The most ambitious time-travel film ever attempted, and the hardest to follow on purpose.
legacyCastNotes: The famous plane crash was a real Boeing 747 — Nolan bought and crashed it.
John David Washington trained with Olympic sprinters for his running style.
The film's soundtrack plays backwards in places, matching the inversion.
Nolan wrote the script over 5 years to make time inversion feel physical.
teaser: Time flows backward. The future is fighting the past. Do not try to understand it, feel it.
facts: The famous plane crash was a real Boeing 747 crashed for the scene.
The film was shot in seven countries including a real 10-minute chase.
Christopher Nolan reportedly wrote the script over several years to make inversion feel physical.
The score by Ludwig Göransson runs partly backwards in places.

title: Mad Max: Fury Road
description: George Miller return to the wasteland after thirty years. Furiosa escapes the tyrant Immortan Joe with his five wives, and Max becomes an unwilling ally in a two-hour chase that never lets go.
legacyCastNotes: Charlize Theron lost her arm prosthetic in the desert and had to shoot on without it for a scene.
Tom Hardy barely spoke to Theron on set — the tension made the film better.
The War Rig is a real vehicle built from a custom chassis with 44-inch wheels.
Most stunts were practical, including a real pole-vaulting rig at 60 mph.
teaser: The world is ash. The war rig is running. Furiosa is driving, and Max is along for the ride.
facts: Most of the stunts were practical, with real cars and real drivers.
The film won six Oscars including editing and production design.
It was storyboarded in detail years before filming.
The War Rig was built as a real vehicle with multiple camera platforms.

title: Deadpool & Wolverine
description: Deadpool is pulled into a mission to save his universe and drags a reluctant Wolverine along. A love letter to Fox Marvel movies, full of cameos, chaos, and surprisingly genuine friendship.
legacyCastNotes: Hugh Jackman wore the yellow-and-blue comic suit for the first time ever.
Ryan Reynolds and Jackman improvised much of their banter.
The cameo cast signed ironclad NDAs — one leaked and got fired from the project.
The film is the first R-rated movie in the MCU.
teaser: The merc with a mouth meets the best there is at what he does. One universe, two legends, zero restraint.
facts: It is the first Deadpool film in the MCU and the only R-rated MCU film.
The film grossed over 1.3 billion dollars.
Hugh Jackman wore the yellow and blue comic suit for the first time.
The cameo list was kept secret and leaked only at release.

title: Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga
description: The prequel to Fury Road, told over fifteen years. Young Furiosa is taken from her home, survives warlords, and slowly becomes the warrior who will drive the War Rig to freedom. Anya Taylor-Joy takes over the role.
legacyCastNotes: Chris Hemsworth gained 30 pounds and shaved his head for Dementus.
Anya Taylor-Joy did 90% of her own driving stunts.
George Miller storyboarded the whole film years before shooting.
The desert scenes were shot in real Australian outback locations.
teaser: Every legend has an origin. Before the War Rig, before the Citadel, there was a girl taken from the Green Place.
facts: Chris Hemsworth shaved his head and gained weight for the villain Dementus.
The film spans fifteen years of Furiosa life in five chapters.
George Miller used a vast miniature landscape for many wide shots.
It was shot on location in Australia over several months.

title: Stranger Things
description: The Duffer Brothers' love letter to 80s Spielberg cinema. In the small town of Hawkins, a group of kids confronts a parallel dimension called the Upside Down, government conspiracies, and their own growing up. The biggest Netflix series of its era.
teaser: A boy vanishes. A girl with a shaved head appears. And something in the Upside Down is waking up.
facts: The show is set in the fictional town of Hawkins, Indiana — inspired by the Duffer Brothers' own childhood.
The Demogorgon costume was a real suit worn by actor Mark Steger.
The kids' bike-riding scenes were shot with camera rigs on actual bikes.
Season 1 was written to work as a miniseries — they never planned a second season.

title: The Last of Us
description: HBO's adaptation of the beloved video game. Joel, a broken smuggler, must escort Ellie, a teenage girl immune to the fungal pandemic, across a ruined America. Craig Mazin (Chernobyl) and the game's creator Neil Druckmann co-wrote it.
teaser: Twenty years after the world fell, a smuggler and a girl cross America. What she carries could save it — or end it.
facts: The infected are based on a real fungus that controls ants' brains.
Pedro Pascal and Bella Ramsey barely knew the game before auditioning.
The mushroom tendrils are practical effects, not CGI.
The show cost over $100 million — one of the most expensive TV seasons ever.

title: Squid Game
description: Netflix's biggest series ever. Desperate people accept a mysterious invitation to play childhood games for a fortune — but losing means dying. A brutal satire of capitalism wrapped in pastel playground colors.
teaser: 456 players. 45.6 billion won. Six children's games. One winner. Everyone else dies.
facts: It became Netflix's most-watched show ever, with 1.65 billion hours in its first month.
The giant doll in 'Red Light, Green Light' is based on a real Korean schoolgirl character.
The set design hides the games in plain sight — the playground is a metaphor for the show itself.
The creator, Hwang Dong-hyuk, wrote the script for over a decade, and it was rejected for years.

title: Parasite
description: Bong Joon-ho's Oscar-winning masterpiece. The Kim family, living in a semi-basement, schemes its way into the employment of the wealthy Park family. A pitch-black comedy, a thriller, and a class-war allegory that ends in one of cinema's great gut-punches.
teaser: A poor family infiltrates a rich one — one job, one lie, one house at a time. Then the basement door opens.
facts: It became the first non-English film to win the Best Picture Oscar.
The house was built as a full set for the film — every floor was real.
Bong Joon-ho said the film is 'a comedy without clowns and a tragedy without villains.'
The staircase motif runs through the whole film — up is wealth, down is poverty.

title: Train to Busan
description: The modern zombie masterpiece. A workaholic father takes his daughter to see her mother in Busan — and the train ride becomes a survival nightmare when a zombie outbreak erupts. A disaster film with a heart the size of Korea.
teaser: A father and daughter board a train to Busan. By the time it arrives, they will have fought through a nation of the dead.
facts: It became the highest-grossing Korean film of 2016 and a global phenomenon.
The zombie makeup took 3 to 4 hours per extra — and hundreds of extras were used.
The train set was built as a full working carriage on a gimbal for the crash scenes.
The film's director, Yeon Sang-ho, was known for animation before this live-action debut.

title: A Quiet Place
description: John Krasinski's brilliant high-concept horror. Blind monsters hunt by sound, and a family must live in total silence — communicating in sign language, walking on sand paths, and keeping the newborn quiet. A film where a single sneeze is a life-or-death moment.
teaser: If they hear you, they hunt you. A family survives in total silence — until the baby comes.
facts: The film is almost dialogue-free — the first act has no spoken words at all.
Millicent Simmonds, who plays the deaf daughter, is deaf in real life and taught the family sign language.
Krasinski wrote the father's story after becoming a parent himself.
The monsters' design was inspired by the creatures in Cloverfield, which Krasinski also appeared in.

title: Hereditary
description: Ari Aster's debut is the most talked-about horror film of the decade. After the matriarch dies, the Graham family unravels as dark secrets surface — miniature dioramas, a cult, and a grief that becomes possession. Hereditary is grief as horror.
teaser: A family grieves. A grandmother's death opens a door — and something that was waiting comes through.
facts: Ari Aster wrote the script after his own grandmother's death — the grief is real.
Toni Collette's performance is widely called one of the best horror performances ever.
The miniature houses in the film were built by a professional miniaturist — and mirror the real sets exactly.
The film was shot in sequence so the family's disintegration felt real.

title: Get Out
description: Jordan Peele's directorial debut — a horror film about race that became a cultural earthquake. Chris goes to meet his girlfriend's parents, and the weekend turns into a nightmare of hypnosis, stolen bodies, and the Sunken Place. Smart, funny, and terrifying.
teaser: A Black man meets his white girlfriend's family. They're very welcoming. Too welcoming.
facts: It was Jordan Peele's directorial debut — he wrote the script in one sitting over a weekend.
The film was made for $4.5 million and grossed $255 million.
Peele was inspired by his own experiences meeting white partners' families.
The 'Sunken Place' scene was originally going to be a full dream sequence.

title: Annihilation
description: Alex Garland's cosmic horror masterpiece. A biologist joins an expedition into 'the Shimmer' — a quarantined zone where DNA is being rewritten. Based on Jeff VanderMeer's novel, the film is about self-destruction, mutation, and what we become.
teaser: A shimmer on the horizon. Five women go in. One comes out. And she is not the same.
facts: The film was nearly shelved — Paramount tested it badly and sold overseas rights to Netflix.
The bear creature was made with practical effects and real bear sounds.
The 'Shimmer' light effects were created with real prisms and lenses, not CGI.
The soundtrack's unsettling choral music was composed by Geoff Barrow and Ben Salisbury.

title: Nosferatu
description: Robert Eggers' gothic masterpiece — the most terrifying Count Orlok ever put on screen. A haunted young woman and the vampire infatuated with her collide in a tale of obsession, plague, and the undead. A 1922 classic reborn in shadows and candlelight.
teaser: A young woman. A vampire. An obsession older than death itself. He is coming — and he will not be refused.
facts: Bill Skarsgård's Orlok was created with prosthetic makeup and a voice lowered in post — almost unrecognizable.
Eggers studied 18th-century Romania and consulted historians for the film's authenticity.
The film was shot almost entirely in real candlelight — no digital lighting.
The rat plague scenes used over 5,000 real trained rats.

title: The Conjuring: The Devil Made Me Do It
description: The third Conjuring film — and the first true story that goes to court. Ed and Lorraine Warren investigate the Arne Johnson case: the first US murder trial where demonic possession was the legal defense. A possession film that becomes a detective story.
teaser: The Warrens take their most dangerous case: a murder trial where the defense is demonic possession.
facts: The film is based on the real 1981 'Devil Made Me Do It' murder case — the first time possession was used as a legal defense in the US.
Patrick Wilson and Vera Farmiga are the only actors to appear in every Conjuring film.
The 'conjuring universe' now spans 8+ films and billions in box office.
The real Ed Warren was a demonologist and author; the film tones down his controversial reputation.
